newsitem.title: CHINA: China not to change export tax rebates in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China not to change export tax rebates in 1997.

text.p: China plans no major changes to its policy on export tax rebates this year, a senior taxation official said on Tuesday.
"Both the rebate rates and the system will remain largely unchanged this year," the Xinhua news agency quoted Cheng Faguang, deputy-director of the State Administration of Taxation, as saying.
"If the policies and detailed operation rules are changed, they will only be made even more to benefit the interest of exporters," he said, but did not elaborate.
China reduced its export tax rebates last year, resulting in a slump in exports for several months.
China would pay all delayed tax rebates to exporters by the end of this year, in line with a State Council, or cabinet, decision at the end of 1995, Cheng said.

The administration would work with other government departments to formulate a set of rules on tax exemptions and rebates for manufacturers that export goods without going through state-run export companies, he said.
Chinese exporters were paid 82.63 billion yuan ($9.9 billion) in tax rebates last year, up 50.5 percent from 1995.
